body:
N-36 NEEDS A RULE FOR A REF HELD BY DESIGN (22 Nov 2026, from the P2-25 slice 4 fix rounds, PR #118; the lead's ruling (a): NOT in that PR, noted here).

N-36's removal trigger is "the worklist (`ref_recheck`) is empty on every install the project knows, and one release has passed". The rehome empties the worklist only for a ref whose every library file it could decide. It deliberately leaves a ref ON the worklist (a wrong move is worse than none) in four cases, and two or three of them can last for good on a Host:
* a file with no usable tags, or the placeholder artist and no id: freed when the Host tags the file or removes it;
* a song that fits a file's tags as well as another song (R has no ISRC, X holds the one the tags carry, R and X share no file so `refmerge` never folds them): freed only when the file is removed or the ISRC is taken out of its tags. Tagging cannot help: the tags are already right. On a Host where that never happens the ref is held FOR GOOD; the same for a song with the same name and another length (freed when its stored length is corrected or the file is removed);
* the last file of a song a person owns: freed when the song gains another file or nobody owns it any more.
On such a Host the worklist never becomes empty, so N-36's trigger NEVER FIRES there, `audit_stack.py check rekey` says FAIL for good, and every pair held for that ref (`recheck_pending`) stays held.

So N-36 needs a rule of its own before it can be built. Options for the lead/advisor to weigh (none is built): (1) after one release, a ref held by design is taken off the worklist and its pairs stay held by a plain reason of their own (so the audit can pass and the module can go; the cost: the hold is then invisible); (2) the trigger is changed from "empty" to "every ref left on it is held by one of the named reasons and its files are listed by the audit" (the cost: the code stays as long as one such ref exists); (3) the Host answers each ref by the audit's list of files (tag, remove, or accept), and an accepted ref leaves the worklist for good. Whichever is chosen, say it in docs/18 ("the rehome") and in docs/tasks/RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md 4b, which today say only that the ref can stay for good.

What the second fix round changed here: nothing about which refs are held; the table of reasons and what lets each go is now ONE table in code (`rehome.HOLDS`), printed by the pass's log line and by the audit's FAIL line, and tested against what the pass does.
